Early and accurate detection through chest X-rays is vital for prompt intervention, complication prevention, and reduced hospital stays. w.r.t the methods employed, this paper presents a novel approach utilizing hybrid algorithms for pneumonia detection from chest X-ray images, combining convolutional neural networks (CNN), VGG16, ResNet152V2, and Gradient Descent optimization. The method involves preprocessing X-ray images to enhance features, followed by feature extraction using both traditional machine learning and deep learning models. Pre-trained models ResNet152V2 and VGG16 are integrated to improve overall system performance. w.r.t. the results, the system automatically extracts features from chest X-ray images using CNNs, enhanced by Gradient Descent optimization to better discriminate between pneumonia patients and healthy cases. Experimental results indicate that the proposed hybrid algorithms significantly outperform traditional approaches, achieving high accuracy in pneumonia detection. Concluding remarks says the study demonstrates the potential of deep learning and hybrid algorithms for more precise and efficient pneumonia diagnosis in clinical settings, highlighting their role in enhancing early and effective medical interventions. These results highlight the potential of hybrid algorithms for improving the diagnosis of pneumonia from chest’s X-ray’s images, thereby aiding in early and effective medical intervention.

articleTitle: A Spectral Learning Enhancement method in Cooperative multiagent system for production control system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: In modern production control systems, efficient management of resources and coordination among multiple agents are crucial for optimizing performance and achieving operational goals. This study introduces the Spectral Learning Enhancement (SLE) method, a novel approach designed to improve decision-making and coordination in cooperative multi-agent systems. The SLE method leverages spectral learning techniques to analyze and enhance the communication and interaction patterns between agents, leading to more informed and adaptive production control strategies. The SLE method integrates spectral graph theory with advanced learning algorithms to model the relationships between agents and their environment. By analyzing the spectral properties of the interaction graph, the method identifies key patterns and dependencies that inform the learning process. This approach allows for the dynamic adjustment of agent behaviors and strategies based on real-time feedback and evolving production conditions. Results from extensive simulations and real-world case studies demonstrate the efficacy of the SLE method. In a controlled production environment, the application of SLE led to a 15% increase in overall system efficiency, as measured by production output and resource utilization. Additionally, the method improved coordination among agents, reducing communication overhead by 20% and minimizing production downtime by 10%. The enhanced adaptability of the agents, driven by the spectral learning framework, resulted in a 25% reduction in response time to unexpected changes in production demands. The SLE method's ability to enhance both individual and collective agent performance positions it as a significant advancement in the field of production control. By incorporating spectral analysis into multi-agent systems, the method provides a robust and scalable solution for optimizing production processes and achieving greater operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of CPUs and GPUs for Training CNN models using Tomato Leaf Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: Plant diseases are a severe threat to plant development and food security, making early detection is crucial for preventive actions. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are considered a promising tool for the automated detection of plant diseases. However, the high computational demands associated with CNN training pose significant challenges, necessitating the importance of selecting hardware platforms carefully for optimal performance and cost-effectiveness. The study evaluates CNN performance on Central Processing Unit (CPU) and Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) platforms for plant disease detection. Key performance metrics including training time, accuracy, memory usage, and throughput are compared between CPU and GPU implementations to evaluate their respective efficiencies. Insights gained from this outcome is that, GPU demonstrate superior performance over CPU by achieving significantly faster training time of 86.27seconds and higher throughput of 87.88 samples/second despite operating at a lower clock speed of 0.000585GHZ. The study underscores the advantage of GPU acceleration for CNN based plant disease detection, offering valuable insights for optimizing real-world implementation.

articleTitle: Visualizing Vitality: Decoding P&ID Connectivity via Symbol Detection and Line Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: The research utilizes YOLOv5 for symbol detection, EasyOCR for text recognition, and the Progressive Probabilistic Hough Transform (PPHT) for identifying straight lines in Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), pivotal blueprints depicting industrial plant piping, instrumentation, and control systems. During the training phase, symbols are meticulously cropped and labeled using an open-source tool. Performance evaluation reveals that early stopping applied to the Group Shuffle Split method achieves an outstanding precision of 93%, surpassing alternative approaches. These results underscore the effectiveness of our sampling and model refinement strategies in optimizing P&ID analysis. Identified texts and symbols are cataloged based on unique IDs, occurrence frequency, and labels, enhancing comprehension crucial for efficient industrial facility operation and maintenance. Additionally, PPHT aids in detecting lines between symbols identified by the YOLOv5 algorithm, further enriching the analysis of P&IDs.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization based Prediction and Ensemble Machine Learning Classification of Wildlife Habitats
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: The accurate classification of wildlife habitats is necessary as it provides necessary resources and condition of wildlife population. To improve this prediction task, the proposed research developed Machine Learning (ML) framework using the remote sensing data. The data is initially pre-processed using Adaptive Histogram Equalization (AHE) and the features such as spectral, special, and texture features are extracted. The features are then selected using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). The features are then optimised using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for optimal prediction and then classified using Ensemble Machine Learning (EML) algorithms such as Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests (RF), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The method showed better capabilities to classify different kinds of wildlife habitats and the values of integrating optimization methods with EML algorithms for solving ecological problems. The experimental results showed that the proposed PSO-EML algorithm achieved better classification accuracy and optimized prediction with an accuracy of 99.61%, and precision of 97.39% when compared to the existing methods Boosted Regression Tree (BRT) and Hierarchical clustering in handling high dimensions and noise features of ecological data.

articleTitle: Stray Lion Optimizer based LSTM Model for Detecting the Fake News
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: Because of the damage it can do to people, communities, and countries, the massive spread of misinformation across many internet stages has develop an urgent issue. In order to address this issue, the scientific community is presently making significant efforts. Fighting disinformation at its earliest stages is difficult since current techniques for detecting fake news overstate the impact of public opinion. In order to address this problematic, the paper suggests a new framework for detecting bogus news using optimizer-based Deep Learning. At first, the d-D feature vectors for the textual data are recovered using the TF-IDF weighting algorithm. The LSTM algorithm is then told to use the retrieved characteristics. To process the parameters of LSTM and extract the n-gram from the text, the Stray Lion Swarm Optimization Algorithm (SLSOA) is used. In order to identify false news, these retrieved traits are then combined. We apply established assessment methods to two real-world datasets of false news and assess the outcomes. Also included are comparisons with other meta-heuristic algorithms and more modern approaches to detecting false news. The outcomes clearly demonstrate that the suggested model outperforms current models on different datasets. LSTM-SLOA attained as 0.9865 and LSTM measure as 0.7414 and then RNN as 0.7525 and also CNN as 0.6381 and then DBN attained as 0.8118 congruently.

articleTitle: PsyNet: A robust Deep Learning-based framework for Detecting Psychiatric Disorders using EEG signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: In the modern world, many people suffer from various psychiatric disorders. Diagnosing psychiatric disorders early increases the chances of full recovery for patients and prevents their health from deteriorating. However, detecting psychiatric disorders early is often difficult. The goal of this paper is to design a novel Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered methodology for detecting different psychiatric disorders by analyzing the EEG (electroencephalography) signals of humans. A deep learning-based classifier model named PsyNet is designed for this purpose. The designed PsyNet model consists of a stacked autoencoder network and an attention mechanism-based proposed PLSTM (Potent Long Short-Term Memory) classifier model. The designed PsyNet model is capable of detecting six different psychiatric disorders, such as addiction disorder, trauma and stress-related disorder, mood disorder, schizophrenia, anxiety-related disorder, and obsessive-compulsive disorder, using the extracted EEG features from the EEG signals of the prefrontal lobe, frontal lobe, parietal lobe, motor cortex, temporal lobe, and occipital lobe. The classification accuracy of the trained PsyNet model is 95.97%. The novelty of this research lies in i) proposing a new architecture of LSTM named PLSTM and using it as a classifier, and ii) incorporating the attention mechanism in the PLSTM classifier network of the PsyNet model to improve its prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Big Data Reasoning enabled Predictive Model in Healthcare Domain for Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: Big data is taking the digital world by a storm and it has its footprints in revolutionizing the healthcare sector. It can be used with various predictive learning based techniques to help in integrating frameworks and providing solutions regarding value based care to identify patients with high risk. It also helps in the diagnosis of the diseases with better statistical outcomes. This study discusses a novel proposed predictive model embedding big data analytics in healthcare domains. The model is based upon an intelligent disease risks detection using explanatory modules to find insights and linkages in data. Further feedback loops are used to gather input and makes modifications to the model to continuously enhance performance. The model provided scalability with a mean CPU usage and bandwidth utilization of 26.48% and 47.2% with increase in data size. Thus, the model can assist the medical experts in efficient and scalable health diagnosis.

articleTitle: Predicting Human Body Prakriti with Ayurvedic Tridosha Features using Ensemble Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: Ayurveda, an ancient medical system, provides insight into personal health through the concept of Prakriti, which determines a person's constitution. Integrating these traditional concepts with modern medical practice is a huge challenge. The research has addressed this problem by developing a machine learning-based Prakriti estimation method. Advanced algorithms, including random forests and ensemble models, were used to analyze a rich dataset of biological traits not easily altered by current cosmetic or technological interventions. This approach achieved a remarkable accuracy of 98\%, validating the effectiveness of integrating machine learning and Ayurvedic principles. Future research will focus on expanding the dataset to include a wider range of biological features and improving feature selection methods to increase the generalizability and applicability of the model in various clinical settings, thereby improving the relationship between traditional Ayurvedic knowledge and modern medical practice. The gap must be narrowed further.

articleTitle: Analysis and Application of Photovoltaic Grid Connection Optimization Model based on LightGBM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: With the increasing popularity of photovoltaic (PV) energy worldwide, the operational efficiency and stability of PV grid-connected systems have become critical issues that need to be addressed.PV grid-connected systems are affected by a variety of factors, such as light intensity, temperature, and aging of the equipment, which may lead to fluctuations in the efficiency of the system, and consequently, affect the stability and reliability of the entire power system. Therefore, how to effectively deal with these challenges and improve the operational efficiency and stability of PV grid-connected systems has become one of the hot topics in current research. In order to cope with the problem of fluctuating efficiency of PV grid-connected system, this paper proposes a PV grid-connected optimisation model based on LightGBM (Light Gradient Boosting Machine) algorithm. The model constructs a corresponding optimisation strategy by deeply analysing the key factors affecting the efficiency of PV grid-connection, such as weather conditions, equipment status, etc. The LightGBM algorithm, with its high efficiency and accuracy, plays an important role in model construction and prediction. The experimental results show that the LightGBM-based PV grid- connected optimisation model proposed in this paper achieves more than 95% in prediction accuracy, which is highly consistent with the actual operation data. More importantly, the operational efficiency of the PV grid-connected system is significantly improved by the optimisation suggestions provided by the model, with an average improvement of about 20%. This finding not only verifies the superiority of the model in prediction accuracy, but also demonstrates its great potential in improving the operational efficiency and stability of the system.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Enhance Influencer Marketing in E-commerce: A Cross-A-Siamese Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: One of the most notable aspects of the Internet is the fact that the cost of (global) communication has been drastically decreased. Individuals may potentially reach massive audiences with their messages over the Internet due to its widespread use. With the rise of blog services, social networking platforms, etc., people's technological talents are no longer a limiting factor. Data preprocessing, feature selection, and model training should all be done in this sequence of significance. Applying fundamental data preparation techniques guaranteed the data's accuracy and relevancy. Feature selection includes the computation of an influencer's overall rank based on six important criteria, which are used for influencer identification and ranking. Feature retrieval is the first step in training Unified Cross-A-Siamese models. The proposed method outperforms two cutting-edge methods: Attention module and siamese. Accuracy increased by 95.70 percent once the approach was used.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Framework for Dynamic Resource Allocation in Malware Analysis Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: The emerging strains of malware demand adaptive cybersecurity systems with the ability to shift resourcefully to performance versus good detection – with optimal resource use, especially as threats quickly evolve. This paper presents a policy using reinforcement learning (RL) for dynamic resource allocation in malware analysis: an RL agent observes files and assigns computer resources based on their potential level of threat. The agent learns by trial and error to give precedence to sample examination while maximizing the usage of resources; the study also describes RL environment design, the structure of the agent, and the reward system. The model has shown good accuracy at different stages which include 96.1% for training, 92.2% for testing, and 90.5% for validation data against previous methods in fast-changing threats circumstances. This continuous learning ability of the model allows it to be effective in the light of new threats, which has helped develop resource-aware, scalable, and adaptable malware analysis systems against changing risks in cybersecurity. This model provides benefits and some of the main challenges in this domain for dynamic malware analysis and resource allocation.

articleTitle: Attack Detection from Internet of Things using TPE based Self-Attention based Bidirectional Long-Short Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: In the realm of cybersecurity, artificial intelligence (AI) emerges as a potent tool for combating cyber threats effectively. By harnessing AI capabilities, cybersecurity teams streamline operations, accelerate threat detection and response, and enhance precision in defensive strategies. The increasing complexity of cyber threats necessitates the development of sophisticated intrusion detection systems (IDSs) This study contributes to the existing cybersecurity knowledge by introducing an advanced Intrusion Detection Scheme tailored for heterogeneous Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks. Leveraging Deep Transfer Learning (DTL), our research enhances IDS capabilities specifically suited for IIoT environments. We employ Self-Attention based Bidirectional Long-Short Term Memory (SA-BiLSTM) to detect attacks, complemented by the Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) for parameter optimization in BiLSTM. Through rigorous evaluation, our architecture consistently achieves an outstanding accuracy rate of approximately 99% in detecting a diverse range of cyberattacks. Notably, our system effectively counters 14 different types of cyber threats, affirming its efficacy in safeguarding IIoT networks. These results underscore the significance of ongoing advancements in creating robust, adaptable, and responsive intrusion detection systems tailored to the intricate landscape of IIoT networks.

articleTitle: NLP for Sentiment Analysis in Social Media Posts to Detect Suspicious Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: In an era where social media is an almost omnipresent means of communication, online safety is crucial. Still, conventional sentiment analysis methods sometimes fall short of accurately spotting dubious conduct. A novel approach utilizing advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, especially Deep Learning (DL) models like BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), is proposed to overcome these challenges. DL is used by the suggested method to identify nuanced attitudes in social media posts, which raises the accuracy of identifying suspicious activities. That is not the case with conventional systems that depend on basic algorithms. With detection rates of 88%, 85%, and 90% for hate speech, violent statements, and extreme opinions, respectively, the system accomplishes remarkable outcomes via meticulous data gathering, preprocessing, and model training. Through comparison, it outperforms existing systems in terms of F1 score (0.92), recall (0.91), precision (0.94), and accuracy (0.92). The proposed system effectively reduces potential risks and encourages a safer online environment by utilizing the effective analysis of sentiment in social media posts, therefore indicating a major advancement in online security.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Non-Destructive Silkworm Cocoon Sex Classification using Machine Learning Models Based on X-Ray and Camera Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: Silk production plays a vital role in global economies, with sericulture heavily dependent on efficient seed production processes. Traditional methods involve manually cutting cocoons to classify silkworm sex, which leads to silk damage, labor intensiveness, and potential inaccuracies. In response, non-destructive technologies like X-ray and camera imaging have emerged, enabling sex classification without cocoon damage, thereby enhancing efficiency and reducing manual errors. This study undertakes a comparative analysis of X-ray and camera imaging methods for silkworm sex classification. X-ray imaging demonstrates superior efficiency in extracting detailed features from silkworm pupae, crucial for accurate classification. In contrast, camera imaging excels in the rapid and cost-effective classification of silkworms based on extracted features. The results reveal significant findings: using X-ray imaging model achieves 97.1% accuracy for FC1 and 96.3% accuracy for FC2, employing ensemble learning technique like AdaBoost. Meanwhile, camera imaging achieves an accuracy above 98% for both FC1 and FC2 using XGBoost, showcasing its effectiveness in real-time classification scenarios. Computational time analysis indicates that X-ray imaging is faster in feature extraction, while camera imaging consumes less memory during classification. These findings underscore the practical advantages of non-destructive imaging technologies and machine learning in revolutionizing sericulture practices. By enhancing productivity and sustainability through accurate sex classification of silkworms, these methods contribute significantly to the growth and efficiency of the silk industry.

articleTitle: Optimized Automated Stock Trading using DQN and Double DQN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: Stock Portfolio management involves managing the buying, holding and selling decisions for the various stocks in the portfolio. There has been work where Reinforcement Learning (RL) based actor-critic methods like Deep Direct Policy Gradient (DDPG) have been used for asset allocation problems. Here an attempt has been made to use solely critic-based value function methods like Deep Q-network (DQN) and Double DQN for estimating Q-values of market actions. Then, an optimized portfolio management algorithm designed to balance trades across a basket of stocks is designed. Five stocks are chosen of different price ranges from NYSE and NASDAQ stock exchanges. The average cumulative percentage returns provided by DQN was 55% on testing data with an average Maximum Drawdown (MDD) of 2.5%. The same with Double DQN was 71% on testing data with an average MDD of 2.83%. These results were significantly better than the case when a traditional Buy and Hold strategy was to be employed.

articleTitle: K-Nearest Neighbor Based High Impedance Fault Detection for Radial Feeder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: In the process of providing electrical supply to rural areas using radial feeders, typical operating voltage levels of 11KV, are commonly utilized. These systems connect the supply from sub-station to the consumer-end through distribution transformers. However, in such configurations, conductors may come into contact with tree branches or other conducting mediums, leading to a type of fault known as High Impedance Fault (HIF). HIFs are characterized by phase-to-ground faults with ground resistance, resulting in low fault currents that resemble the load current carrying capacity. These faults pose significant danger to living organisms and cannot detected due to their non-linear nature. This paper proposes a model employing a multilayer perceptron artificial neural network (ANN) and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) for the detection of HIFs in radial feeders. The proposed KNN method has achieved better results by assigning k = 2 in predicting the fault bus. The proposed model efficacy is demonstrated using the IEEE 13 bus radial distribution test system.

articleTitle: Advanced Three-Phase Plls for Grid Synchronization in the Application of Power Quality Compensators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Algorithms for Computational Intelligence Systems (IACIS)
abstract: Effective techniques for extracting the fundamental frequency positive sequence (FFPS) component are crucial for integrating renewable energy sources (RESs) and enhancing the disturbance rejection capability of synchronous reference frame frequency-locked loop (SRF-FLL) systems under diverse grid conditions. This paper offers a concise overview and assessment of phase-locked loop (PLL) techniques. It then provides a comparison and selection guide to assist in choosing the suitable PLL for specific applications, aiming to enhance the control and integration of RESs in power systems.
